items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Charlie Shavers was dying of cancer and was starting to miss a lot of gigs. So Shavers called Taft to fill in for him. And Taft said, “No, but call my student.” And I said, “Mr. Shavers, it’s a real honor, but they expect to hear you, and if they get me they’re not going to be happy.”

ctx.x: How did they get you up there?

What happened was a drunk wanted Milestones. And you know you have a lot of options when you have a drunk and one of them is see if you can probably get rid of him with sweetness rather than vinegar. I mean that was one of the great night club rules. You know like not that we had too many bouncing problems there, but the trick there is if you’ve got to put somebody out in the street bodily okay cool, you earned your pay. But if I think that’s the way he’s going out and you talk him out, that’s a twenty dollar tip…
had to say yes regardless of consequences. So I said no, so obviously I knew what the answer was.
